title: Calling scalar methods (`scalar()`,`scalar_one_or_none()`,`scalar_one()`) causes runtime exception due to missing `_source_supports_scalars` attribute
body:
### Describe the bug

Calling scalar methods (`scalar()`,`scalar_one_or_none()`,`scalar_one()`) causes runtime exception due to missing `_source_supports_scalars` attribute

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncResult.scalar

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.38

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

asyncpg

### Database Vendor and Major Version

PostgreSQL 15

### Python Version

3.12

### Operating system

MacOS Sequoia 15.3

### To Reproduce

```python
import asyncio
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy import text

engine = create_async_engine("postgresql+asyncpg://scott:tiger@localhost:5432/postgres", echo=True)

async def main():
    async with engine.connect() as conn:
        async_result = await conn.stream(text("SELECT 1,'hello world'"))
        scalar = await async_result.scalar() # Error here
        print(scalar)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

```
AttributeError: 'AsyncResult' object has no attribute '_source_supports_scalars'
``` 

### Additional context

IMHO I think these methods should be deprecated because it doesn't really make sense doesn't really make sense for someone to ever stream a single row, hence why nobody has run into this issue before, but I'm guessing these methods exist to maintain an identical if not very similar API interface with respect to the Result object. Therefore, if the interface exists it probably should work
